title: Analytics tool: from per-seat to usage-based pricing
question: What could happen if a small analytics tool moves from per-seat pricing to usage-based pricing?

documents.name: 01-pricing-memo.md
documents.content:
# Pricing memo: from seats to usage

This is a fictional memo written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Proposal

Tallybeam, a small analytics tool, charges $18 per seat per month. The product team proposes charging by the number of reports run each month instead, with the first 200 reports free. Annual contracts would stay on seats until they renew.

## Why

Most revenue comes from teams of two to ten seats, and many of those seats are occasional users. The finance lead says annual churn of paid accounts was 9% last year. The product lead expects usage pricing to make the tool easier to adopt inside a team, and the finance lead expects it to make monthly revenue harder to forecast.

## Timing

The billing system cannot meter reports until the third quarter. A pilot with new customers only is proposed for the quarter after that.

documents.name: 02-customer-interviews.md
documents.content:
# Customer interview notes

This is a fictional set of notes written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Who was interviewed

Twelve customers were interviewed, chosen by the account team. Seven are on annual contracts and five pay monthly.

## What they said

Small teams said they like paying only for what they use. Two larger customers said their finance departments need a predictable invoice and would not accept a variable bill without a cap. A reseller said it quotes clients a fixed annual price and would need a cap or a bundle. An education customer said its grant rules require a fixed budget line for software.

## Gaps

Nobody was asked how many reports a typical user runs. The team has no data on the spread of usage across customers.

documents.name: 03-finance-and-contracts-note.md
documents.content:
# Finance and contracts note

This is a fictional note written for an evaluation. All names, places and figures are invented.

## Churn and revenue

The account team reports that annual churn of paid accounts was 14% last year.

## Contracts

Annual contracts include a price lock until renewal, so customers on them cannot be moved to usage pricing before then. Invoices to customers in the European market must show value-added tax, and the billing platform does not yet support per-report tax lines.

## Support

The support team has not been told about the change. A change in how invoices are calculated usually produces a rise in billing questions in the first two months.
